description: 1U one- or two-socket AMD EPYC rack server, 16th generation. Up to ten 2.5 inch front drive bays, or eight with a Smart Flow vent, four 3.5 inch, fourteen or sixteen EDSFF E3.S, or none. Two 60 mm power supplies stand at opposite ends of the rear. It has up to three PCIe slots, an OCP NIC 3.0 slot, an optional LOM card and a rear BOSS-N1 boot module.

gaps.note: ISM table 101 and TG table 17 list configuration 0 (no riser, no PCIe slots), but the one figure of it - TG figure 6, "Rear view of the system with no risers" - draws the three-slot rear of figure 6 with its slot fillers and not a blank plate across the riser band, so it cannot be told from configuration 1 with empty slots. The R660's no-riser rear is drawn from a sibling's figure of a different plate; this model does not borrow it. ISM figures 126 to 129 remove "riser blanks" 1 to 4 without a straight-on view.
gaps.wanted: a straight-on rear photograph or drawing of an R6625 with no risers fitted

gaps.note: ISM table 101 lists configuration 8 (R2A + R4 E3 paddle card, two processors) and tables 111 and 112 give 9 (R2A + R4-SCM G5x4 paddle) and 10 (R2A + R4 paddle); the technical guide's tables 12, 17 and 18 stop at 7 and skip 6. Their rear is riser 2A with a blank where riser 3 would be, the face of configuration 7 (one processor), and the R4 paddle card is a cabled board no figure shows. No figure draws them, and a build per paddle card would repeat configuration 7's face.
gaps.wanted: a drawing of riser 4's paddle card and of what the rear shows with it

gaps.note: the straight-on rears the ISM and technical guide draw are configuration 1 (R2A + R3A, figure 6), configuration 5's rear drive module (figure 7) and configuration 6's E3.S module (figure 9). The faces of risers 2P, 3P, 2Q, 1P, 4P, 2S and 3S are the shared 16th-generation risers' (drawn for the R660 from its own figures); the R6625's figures 115 to 124 show them in isometric and agree on their slots and slot numbers. Their top-view outlines are the R660's estimates.
gaps.wanted: straight-on rear photographs of an R6625 in riser configurations 2, 3, 4 and 6

gaps.note: ISM figures 20 and 21 number the 10 and 8 bay builds; no figure held numbers the 4 x 3.5 inch bays, and figure 1 resolves no printing on the face.
gaps.wanted: a straight-on photograph of a 4 x 3.5 inch R6625 front, or the service label of that build

gaps.note: ISM figures 4 and 5 and TG figures 4 and 5 resolve no printing on the E3.S fronts, and the ISM's service labels (figures 20 and 21) are the 2.5 inch builds'. The ids number down each column, as the R660's photographed lip prints; nothing is drawn.
gaps.wanted: a straight-on photograph of an E3.S R6625 front, or its service label

gaps.note: Direct Liquid Cooling is an option (ISM figures 8 and 12, tables 8 and 9): the rear I/O board has no VGA and two coolant tubes leave beside PSU 2, and the top view shows cold plates over the SP5 sockets with a tube route. dell/rear-io-board-dlc-16g@1 (drawn from this ISM's figure 8) exists, but a DLC build's top view needs cold plates on the R6625's own sockets, which no figure dimensions, so no DLC build is offered rather than one whose top view still shows heatsinks.
gaps.wanted: the R6625's DLC cold plates' outline from above, with a height

gaps.note: dell/r6625-air-shroud@1 is a plain 428 x 57.8 band read off ISM figures 10 and 41 and the technical guide's interior render; the moulding is stepped and the figures do not resolve its outline. ISM figure 11 draws the place bare.
gaps.wanted: a top-down view of the shroud fitted, at a scale

gaps.note: ISM table 10 and TG table 28 give the 0-drive build 700.7 mm from ear to rear wall against 751.48 for the 4, 8 and 10 drive builds (50.8 shorter), and the 14 and 16 E3.S builds are in neither row. This device has one depth, 773.5, for every front.
gaps.wanted: the chassis drawing's rows for the E3.S builds, and a one-depth decision

gaps.note: TG table 15 lists the OCP 3.0 cards 2VY37 (Broadcom, 2 x QSFP56, 100 GbE) and FD63G (Mellanox, 2 x SFP56) and "100 GbE" in table 16, while ISM table 21 and TG table 30 give the OCP card as "1 GbE x 4, 10 GbE x 2, 10 GbE x 4, 25 GbE x 2, 25 GbE x 4" and the MIC as 25 or 100 GbE x 2. The ISM governs: the OCP bay accepts the 1, 10 and 25 GbE cards and the blank, and not dell/ocp3-2x100g-qsfp56@1. The ISM adds that the board's OCP width is x8.
gaps.wanted: Dell's statement of which of the two tables is current

gaps.note: the spec sheet's rear bays row reads "Up to 2 x E3.S NVMe direct drives max 15.36.8 TB" (a typo), lists its 1800 W supply as Titanium (ISM table 13) where TG table 33 says Platinum, gives slot 3 as Gen4 only where ISM table 100 gives R3P and R3S as Gen5, and its front-bay list stops at 10 x 2.5 inch SAS, SATA or NVMe (8 x 2.5 inch NVMe is in the ISM's table 74). The ISM's figures are used throughout; none of these changes a drawn dimension.
gaps.wanted: nothing - recorded so the next reader does not take the spec sheet's version

gaps.note: the ISM's "Rail sizing and rack compatibility matrix" section and the TG's rails section (figures 22 to 35) point to Dell's separate Enterprise Systems Rail Sizing and Rack Compatibility Matrix, which is not among the three documents held, so no `chassis.ears` position or rail kit is listed (as on dell/r660 and dell/r740xd).
gaps.wanted: Dell's Enterprise Systems Rail Sizing and Rack Compatibility Matrix

gaps.note: the riser cages are the R660's (the same contracts), so their plates are drawn 1.0 proud of the rear wall, and a seated card's bracket flange stands past the wall with the part of the riser that covers it. The flange is the bracket's own 9.4 return flange (std/pcie-bracket-lp@1, PCIe CEM 5.0 figure 11-9) and the cover is each cage's `flange-cover` node, a column the flange ends sit behind, as the R740xd draws its riser shroud. A rear bay cannot recess its occupant, so the flange stands 9.4 past the wall in a configuration with such a card seated, and a filler's bracket gets the cover as a card's does. The cover's reach (19.3, and 19.2 for the 3-lp cages) is the R660 service model's, carried to this server as an estimate: no model of this server is held and its own chassis table was not re-read for the wall.
gaps.wanted: Dell's R6625 service model, for the covers' reach

boss.description: the BOSS-N1 boot module bay at the far left of the rear

covers.description: the system cover and the backplane cover on top, and the optional security bezel on the front. The bezel is DRAWN FITTED, as on the R660: it is `mounts`, so the viewer takes it off to show the drives, and `for:` names what it covers.

drives.description: the ten 2.5 inch front bays, numbered as the service label prints them (ISM figure 20)

drives-e3s.description: the EDSFF E3.S front bays, numbered down each column (see e3s-numbering)

drives-lff.description: the four 3.5 inch front bays, numbered from the left

drives-rear.description: the two rear 2.5 inch bays of riser configuration 5, where riser 2 would be

attrs.redundancy-note: R6625 technical guide, thermal features: "The PowerEdge R6625 allows N+1 fan redundancy, allowing continuous operation with one fan failure in the system" (a second bullet adds "with >4 fans", which the four dual-rotor modules the ISM's cooling fan table counts satisfy). The ISM adds that for certain single-processor builds three sets are enough, with a fan blank closing bay 1.

fillers.description: the E3.S centre vent and the 14-drive build's two-slot filler

interior.description: the system board, the air shroud and the fan bracket

lom-card.description: the LOM card position. The group holds the card, not its two ports, as the R740xd's NDC group does: the ports are the card's own.

marks.description: printed marks seated as parts - the VGA symbol

memory.description: the 24 DDR5 sockets, named as Dell's memory label prints them (ISM figure 101), twelve per processor - CPU 2's B slots on the left, CPU 1's A slots on the right, seen from above with the rear at the top

panels.description: the left control panel, a field-replaceable module in the left ear

ports.description: the front VGA, the USB-A and the iDRAC Direct micro-AB USB

processors.description: the two processor heatsinks - CPU 1 on the right as the front faces you

attrs.redundancy-note: R6625 ISM table 13 and the spec sheet: two hot-swap supplies, "hot swap redundant"; one supply runs the system.

psus.description: the two 60 mm supplies, PSU 1 at the left as the rear faces you

rear-io.description: the rear I/O board position - the board carries the ID button, the iDRAC port, two USB and the VGA, which are its own ports

riser-blanks.description: the vented plate where riser 3 is absent

risers.description: the expansion card riser positions, numbered as the ISM's riser section numbers the risers (1 and 4 only in the full-height layout). `service` and not `traffic`: the group holds the riser, and the cards live in the riser's own slot bays, numbered as the riser prints them.

tags.description: the slide-out Express Service Tag under the right-hand drive columns (ISM tables 1 to 5, item 5). The E3.S fronts seat it where the 2.5 inch fronts do: their figures list it, and show it there.

name: r6625

bezel.note: DRAWN FITTED, as on the R660, and taken off in the viewer: the optional security bezel (dell/bezel-1u-16g@1; the spec sheet and ISM list a security bezel and an LCD bezel, and the ISM's "Removing the front bezel" shows the same moulding) covers the body between the ears, and `for:` names the bays and parts behind it. Its openings are holes, so the drives show through. 35.84 ear to front with it, 22.0 without (ISM table 10). The LCD bezel is not modelled.

chassis.note: datasheet - ISM table 10 and TG table 28 (the same figures): width 434.0 between the ears (Xb) and 482.0 across them (Xa), height 42.8 (Y). DEPTH 773.5 is the front face to the rear wall: the ears sit 22.0 behind the front face without the bezel (Za, 35.84 with it) and the rear wall 751.48 behind the ears (Zb, for the 4, 8 and 10 drive builds), 773.48 in all. The PSU handles stand a further 35.57 proud (Zc, 787.05 ear to handle), which is the spec sheet's 809.05 without the bezel (22.0 + 787.05), and its 822.89 with the bezel is 13.84 more. The 0-drive build is 50.8 shorter (Zb 700.7) and is not this depth; see the front-nobp note. Weight 20.4 kg fully populated and 15.8 kg without drives and supplies (ISM table 11). The R6625 shares the 16th-generation 1U chassis of the R660, whose Dell-published figures are the same to 0.01 mm.

drive-bays-sff.note: drawing - ISM figures 2 and 3. Five columns 73.0 wide at x 32.5, 115.35, 198.2, 281.1 and 363.95 (an 82.85 pitch) and two rows 15.3 tall at y 7.71 and 24.21: the carrier, common/drive-carrier-25@2, laid flat with rotate 270. The ISM's drives are standard 2.5 inch carriers, and the figure's carriers (rails 7.3 to 22.4 and 23.7 to 38.3 mm) fit the rows.

drive-default.note: EVERY BAY DEFAULTS TO A BLANK: Dell publishes no default drive count, and the ISM requires blanks in every empty slot for cooling (ISM, "Drive blank"). A populated machine is a configuration.

drive-numbering.note: drawing - the service label of ISM figure 20 numbers the 10-bay build 0 and 1, 2 and 3, 4 and 5, 6 and 7, 8 and 9 (upper bay even, lower odd, column by column), and figure 21 numbers the 8-bay build 0-3 then 4-7 around the vent. The front figures themselves resolve no printing on the dividers, so none is drawn: the ids and `rel-pos` carry Dell's numbering.

e3s-fronts.note: drawing - ISM figures 4 and 5 (2.878 px/mm). Each carrier is found by its orange chevrons: columns at x 36.3, 117.3, 280.3 and 361.3, each carrier 77.65 wide and 7.75 tall, with the centre vent at 197.5 to 276.5 - dell/r660's grid laid over figure 5 lands on every carrier, the vent and the last column's end (which, as there, reaches the VGA plate's edge). THE ROWS ARE NOT READ: the figures' vertical scale is not trusted (see gate-1), so the rows' 9.51 pitch (3.17, 12.68, 22.29 and 31.8) is carried from the R660 and checked only to the 1.2 mm the overlay shows. The 14-drive front's last column ends in a two-slot filler below its first two carriers, as figure 4 draws it. The top vent strip is left off: neither figure draws one over E3.S carriers.

e3s-numbering.note: estimated - the figures resolve no printing on the E3.S fronts' lower lip, and no other document held numbers the bays. The ids run e3s-0 to e3s-15 down each column in turn (0-3 under the first, 4-7, 8-11, 12-15), the order dell/r660's photographed lip prints; nothing is drawn on the face. See the e3s-bay-numbers gap.

front-face.note: THE EARS CARRY THE CONTROL PANELS, SO THEY ARE DRAWN - ISM tables 1 to 5 list the left control panel (system health, system ID and status LEDs) and the right control panel (power button, USB, iDRAC Direct) as front features, and both figures draw them in the ears outboard of the drives. The front is therefore the 482.6 rack face.

front-nobp.note: estimated - the no-backplane front is listed (ISM table 10 and TG table 11 give the 0-drive build; ISM figure 20 draws its front) but Dell draws it only as the schematic of the service label, 1.81 px/mm, which resolves three grilles at the left (x 37.7 to 93.2, 121.3 to 176.6 and 204.7 on), a wide grille at the upper right (282.3 to 432) and two lower-right blocks, each within about 3 mm of the dell/r660 front this model carries its grille panels and hole pitch from (5.47 and 5.69 by 5.42, 4.05 x 4.03 holes). The holes are therefore a carried pitch, not a reading. That chassis is 50.8 shorter (ISM table 10, 700.7 ear to rear wall) and this device has one depth.

fronts.note: SIX FRONTS, EACH ITS OWN VIEW bound by `configurations.<name>.views`, as the R660's are. All share the ears, both control panels and the right panel. ISM figures 1 to 5 and 20 draw them: 10 x 2.5 inch (the default `front`, figure 3); 8 x 2.5 inch with the Smart Flow vent (front-sff8sf, figures 2 and 21), the 10-drive front less the middle column, which is a vent plate 78.25 x 33.26 with eight openings, the dividers numbering 0-3 then 4-7; 4 x 3.5 inch (front-lff4, figure 1); no backplane (front-nobp, figure 20); and 14 and 16 x EDSFF E3.S (front-e3s14 and front-e3s16, figures 4 and 5). ISM table 74 lists five backplanes: 4 x 3.5 inch SAS or SATA, 8 x 2.5 inch NVMe, 10 x 2.5 inch, and 14 and 16 x E3.S.

gate-1.note: Gate 1 on ISM figures 1 to 3, extracted at 300 dpi (1650 x 372 px): the silhouette reads 1577 x 139 px, an aspect of 11.35 against 482.6 / 42.8 = 11.28 - 0.6% - so the figures are drawn ear to ear at true scale, 3.268 px/mm across, and every front position here is read off them. The rear figures (6 to 9) draw the 434 body: 1401 x 138 px against 434 / 42.8 = 10.14 (0.1%), 3.225 px/mm. The two E3.S fronts (figures 4 and 5, 1602 x 410 px) are drawn smaller, 2.878 px/mm, and their vertical scale is not trusted (the silhouette reads 118 px for 42.8 mm, 2.757 px/mm), so their rows are carried from the 2.5 inch fronts' row pitch (see e3s-fronts).

lff-front.note: drawing - ISM figure 1 (4 x 3.5 inch, 10 TB SATA carriers). Four columns of common/drive-carrier-35@1, which is drawn wide (105.5 x 26.9) and so stands un-rotated: x 29.2, 136.4, 243.6 and 350.8 (a 107.2 pitch, the R740xd's 3.5 inch column pitch of 107.208, read here from the lamp panels and the rails' ends at 3.268 px/mm to about 1 mm) and y 13.7. The rails of the first and fourth carriers end at x 130.7 and 450.0 in the figure. The VGA connector is NOT in the right control panel on this front: figure 1 draws it in the top strip above the fourth drive (callout 3), a horizontal DE-15 at x 395.6, y 2.2 with the monitor mark at 418.3 to its right, on a textured plate 380.9 to 430.0 wide. The right control panel and the Express Service Tag are the 2.5 inch fronts'. The top strip is a grille of cells on a 5.46 pitch in five runs (x 59.5, 182.0, 288.5, 339.5 and 431.5), with a latch plate carrying a slot at x 40.8 and another at 169.6 and two pairs of small square latches at 281.1 and 331.4, all read off the figure at 6.2 px/mm and good to about 0.7 mm. The cell height, 8.2, is the figure's opening (y 2.7 to 10.9).

lff-numbering.note: estimated - no figure held prints the 3.5 inch bays' numbers (ISM figures 20 and 21 are the 2.5 inch builds'). Dell numbers the 2.5 inch bays 0 and up from the left, so the ids run drive-0 to drive-3 left to right; nothing is drawn on the face. See the lff-bay-numbers gap.

rear.note: drawing - ISM figures 6 to 9 and TG figure 6, the 434 body at 3.225 px/mm. THE REAR MASTERS' FRAME IS THE R660'S: dell/r660's boss, supply, OCP, LOM, rear I/O and riser bays laid over figure 6 and over figure 7 land on the figure's boot module, supplies, OCP bracket, LOM and iDRAC RJ45 openings, USB stack, VGA shell and riser windows (see the-r660-agrees). Positions: PSU 1 at x 33.06 and PSU 2 at 367.91, 59.8 wide; the OCP bay 164.95 wide 71.8; the LOM window 110.59 to 153.17 and the rear I/O window 250.5 to 335.87, y 24.71 to 40.64; the system ID button 252.43.

rear-boss-bay.note: drawing - the boot module bay, 29.9 x 38.9 at x 0.85, the R660's, which ISM figure 6 overlays to about 1.5 mm (the BOSS-N1 module and its blank).

rear-drives.note: drawing - riser configuration 5's two rear 2.5 inch drive bays (ISM figure 7, TG figure 7): 79.25 x 18.0 at x 111.12 and 190.83, y 2.1, laid flat as at the front and carried from the R660, whose bays figure 7 confirms to about 1 mm (the left carrier's body 109.7..182.7, the right 188.8..263.0). They seat the same common/drive-carrier-25@2 as the front; the rear module's bay is larger than the carrier, so the carrier sits centred with the module's frame round it. Riser configuration 6's two rear E3.S drives are in riser 2S (ISM figure 9, TG figure 8).

rear-ism-numbering.note: datasheet - THE ISM NUMBERS THE RISERS TWICE. Its rear-view tables (6 to 9) call the left-hand riser "PCIe expansion card riser 1" and the right-hand "riser 2", while its expansion-card section (figures 115 to 124, tables 100 to 112) calls the left one riser 2 (slots 1 and 2) and the right one riser 3 (slot 3), with risers 1 and 4 the full-height pair, and the risers' names (R2A, R3A, R2P, R3P, R1P, R4P, R2Q, R2S, R3S) agree with the second. The riser section governs here, as on the R660: the left riser is riser 2, the right riser 3.

rear-lom-and-io.note: drawing - the LOM card and the rear I/O board are bays, each the window the figure shows - x 110.59 to 153.17 and 250.50 to 335.87, y 24.71 to 40.64 - and each module carries its own connectors. ISM figure 182 removes "the LOM card and rear I/O board" and figure 186 the MIC card: they are field-replaceable, as on the R660.

rear-power.note: chassis.power is `ac`: every supply this device accepts is an AC mixed-mode unit (800, 1100 and 1400 W, C14: ISM table 13 and 14). The 1100 W -48 V DC, the 1400 W 277 V and 336 V DC and the 1800 W (C15) supplies are not modelled, and when they are, power moves onto per-build configurations. 700 W, which the R660 has, is not in the R6625's tables and is not accepted.

rear-risers.note: drawing - the riser bays are each riser's extent: riser 2 107.0..270.6 and riser 3 270.6..362.6, read on figures 6 and 7 (the overlay lands the riser windows to 1.5 mm), riser 3 listed before riser 2 so riser 2's cage covers the end of slot 3's bracket tip. Riser 2Q 107.0..293.5 and risers 1 and 4 107.0..227.6 and 227.6..362.6 are the R660's, carried because no straight-on R6625 figure draws those risers (ISM figures 115 to 124 show them in isometric); all are at y 2.2, 19.8 tall. Figure 6 (R2A + R3A) and figure 7 (R3P with the rear drive module) are the only straight-on rears besides figure 9's E3.S module; the other risers' faces are the shared 16th-generation risers' (see the riser-faces-shared gap).

rear-slot-numerals.note: drawing - the slot numbers are printed on the riser cages, not the chassis, so they are drawn by the cages and move with the configuration. ISM figures 116 to 124 number the slots: riser 1P slot 1, riser 2Q slots 1 and 2, riser 2A slots 1 and 2, riser 2P slots 1 and 2, riser 3A and 3P slot 3, riser 4P slot 2, riser 3S slot 3, riser 2S slot 1 (TG figure 18 prints riser 3A's as "Slot 2", which is a typo against its own table 18).

right-side.note: drawing - ISM figures 2 and 3: the VGA module is the plate at x 436.95..457.15 carrying a vertical DB-15 and its monitor mark, and the right control panel in the ear carries the power button at the top, a vertical USB-A, and the iDRAC Direct micro-AB USB with its lamp below (ISM tables 1 to 5, item 4 and 3; the USB trident and the iDRAC Direct mark are in the figures). The parts seated there are the library's own, dell/power-button-14g@1 and the std/ ports, centred on the positions the overlay confirms.

sides-and-bottom.note: estimated - no figure held shows the bottom or either side; their folded edges and the rail land are plausible shapes at plausible sizes, drawn so the faces are not blank, and marked estimated where drawn.

the-r660-agrees.note: WHERE A POSITION IS CARRIED FROM dell/r660, IT WAS CHECKED AGAINST THIS DOCUMENT FIRST. The R6625's front is the R660's: laying dell/r660's ear, vent-strip, drive-column and right-panel coordinates over ISM figure 3 at 3.268 px/mm, and its E3.S bay grid over figure 5, puts every edge on its feature to within about 1.2 mm, the resolution of the figure; laid over the rear figures 6 and 7 at 3.225 px/mm, its supply, riser, OCP, LOM, rear I/O and boot bays land the same way, to the same 1.5 mm. The R660 numbers are finer than these figures' resolution, so they are used where the overlay agrees, and the R6625's own reading is used where it does not (the 3.5 inch bays and the VGA connector of that front, and the top view's board, heatsinks, DIMM sockets, fans and shroud).

top.note: drawing - ISM figure 11 (the interior from above, a straight-on render, 1557 x 1918 px) read at 2.189 px/mm (the 434.0 body at 950 px; the ear-to-ear front at 1057 px agrees to 0.1%) with a 10 mm grid laid over it, cross-checked against ISM figures 10 and 101 and the technical guide's interior render. REAR AT y=0, FRONT AT y=773.5 - the library's plan convention; plan x runs left to right as the body is seen from above, so processor 2 and the B memory slots are on the left. The system board is the PCB's outline (421 x 341.7, narrower at the rear); the two heatsinks 92.7 x 144.3 over the AMD SP5 sockets; the 24 DDR5 sockets (twelve per processor: six at the left, twelve between the heatsinks, six at the right) named from the memory label (ISM figure 101, tables 95 and 96); the four dual fan modules and their bracket (the R660's parts: the ISM's cooling-fan table gives the same four dual-rotor modules), the air shroud, the system cover and the drive backplane cover. SEATED MODULES PROJECT INTO THIS VIEW through their rear or front bay's `plan:`: the supplies (dell/psu-60mm-plan@1), the BOSS-N1 module, the OCP card, the LOM card, the rear I/O board, the risers and the upper row of front 2.5 inch drives, at the R660's positions, which ISM figure 11 confirms for the supplies, risers 2 and 3 and the boot module (see the-r660-agrees: the rear faces of the two machines coincide). A blank seats no plan, so the default build shows the two supplies and the two risers. NOT YET IN THIS VIEW: the cards, the drive backplane, the cabling and the PERC modules, and the Direct Liquid Cooling module.

top-dimm-sockets.note: drawing - ISM figure 101 and tables 95 and 96, read with figure 11: the sockets (with their latches) run from plan y 260.3 to 414.7, 154.4 long; the module is the JEDEC DDR5 RDIMM's 133.4 inside it, centred, so each bay is common/dimm-plan@1's 3.8 x 133.4 at y 270.8 and 1.35 in from its socket's left edge. Pitch 8.3 (8.32 left, 8.28 middle, 8.30 right: the figure resolves about 0.1). Socket left edges 17.0 + 8.32k at the left (processor 2's B11 B7 B9 B3 B5 B1), 168.55 + 8.28k in the middle (B2 B6 B4 B10 B8 B12, then processor 1's A11 A7 A9 A3 A5 A1) and 369.5 + 8.30k at the right (A2 A6 A4 A10 A8 A12). The names are read from figure 101's leader lines, which stair-step so the lowest (or, at the rear, highest) label belongs to the outermost socket of its run.

top-fans.note: drawing - the four dual fan modules' housings in figure 11 read x 24.4 to 109.6, 111.5 to 198.0, 237.0 to 322.3 and 323.8 to 410.0 (about 85.5 wide, plan y 471.8 at the rear edge to 558 at the front of the orange handle). The part is dell/fan-1u-16g@1, 82.0 wide, its rotors only, so each is centred on its housing: x 26.0, 113.75, 238.65 and 325.9, y 478.0, good to about 2 mm. The fan bracket and the covers are carried from the R660 (the bracket's front edge at plan y 558.8 is the housings' front edge, the backplane cover's rear edge at 585.3 the technical guide's cover edge, to about 1 mm).

vent-strip.note: drawing - the 2.5 inch fronts' row of 4.05 x 2.33 slots on a 5.46 pitch along the top edge, y 3.08, in groups of three and six: laid over ISM figure 3 at 2x, each of the fifty-three slots lands on a dark opening of the figure's strip. The master-style gaps where the figure draws a slot lighter (closed) are left out.
